title: The Little Book of Semaphores
byline: Allen B. Downey · Green Tea Press, 2nd edition
note: Most problems are presented as puzzle, hint and solution over several pages; the leaves here cover all three. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A puzzle book for learning concurrent programming with one primitive, the semaphore. After defining semaphores and the execution model, Downey builds the standard patterns (signaling, rendezvous, mutex, multiplex, barriers, queues) and then works through dozens of synchronization problems: the classics (producer–consumer, readers–writers, dining philosophers, cigarette smokers), lesser-known ones (barbershops, Santa Claus, H₂O, river crossing, roller coaster) and his own inventions (sushi bar, senate bus, Faneuil Hall). Each problem is posed, hinted and solved in Python-like pseudocode, with attention to deadlock, starvation and fairness. The last chapters translate the ideas into real Python and C with POSIX threads.
